To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the encapsulation ability of cyclodextrin-based polymers is highly dependent on the degree of crosslinkage, and that this is a result of structural homogeneity and mobility.
the encapsulation ability of CDPs toward BPA in aqueous media strongly depends on the chain length of the crosslinkers.
the encapsulation abilities of the CDPs depend on the degree of crosslinkage and the chain lengths of their crosslinking agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization, and molecular dynamics of CDPs crosslinked by PEGDE, as well as their encapsulation ability toward hydrophobic molecules.
the preparation of water-insolubilized CD polymers, the effects of crosslinking agents on the structure and encapsulation ability, and the encapsulation of BPA in aqueous media.
the synthesis of CDPs with various degrees of crosslinkings by different chain lengths of PEGDE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the encapsulation ability of CDPs is governed by both the degree of crosslink and the chain lengths of crosslinking agents.
CDPs crosslinked by long PEGDE chains are suitable for use as a BPA encapsulation agent.
the CDPs with a high degree of crosslinkage have a dense and highly rigid structure, which is responsible for their high encapsulation abilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CDPs with low degrees of crosslink by PEGDE would be suitable for the removal of BPA in water, whereas CDPs with high degrees of crosslinks by PEGDE could be used for the encapsulation of BPA in the solid phase.
a CDP sample with an appropriate degree of crosslinkage by a crosslinking agent with a suitable chain length can encapsulate a target molecule with high efficiency.
the crosslinking degree and chain lengths of the PEGDE play an important role in determining the structural homogeneity, mobility, and BPA encapsulation ability of CDPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the encapsulation ability of the CDPs is strongly affected by the chain lengths of their crosslinking agents.
the CDP with a low degree (≤ 1.2) of crosslinking using PEGDE is a promising material for use in encapsulating hydrophobic molecules in an aqueous medium.
a CDP with a low degree crosslinking by long-chain crosslinking agent can be used as a potential carrier to encapsulate BPA molecules in aqueous media.
